newsitem.title: CHINA: HK dollar "rock solid" - Financial Secretary Tsang.
newsitem.headline: HK dollar "rock solid" - Financial Secretary Tsang.

text.p: The Hong Kong dollar was "rock solid" and faced no threat following the sharp drop in the value of the Thai baht, Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said on Thursday.

"As far as the Hong Kong dollar is concerned, let me assure you it is rock solid," Tsang said. "The Hong Kong government has not been in the market. The Hong Kong dollar is still trading on the strong side of the link."
The local unit is pegged at HK$7.8 to U$1.0 and floats in a narrow band around that level. It was trading at HK$7.7430/40 late Thursday.

Tsang said Hong Kong was in a very different situation compared to other economies, with healthy foreign reserves, a conservative fiscal system with sustained budget surpluses, and world class banking and regulatory structures.
"I do not see the threat at all," he added.
Hong Kong had foreign reserves of US$66.6 billion at the end of May and a fiscal 1996/97 budget surplus of HK$25.7 billion.
The Thai baht lost 15-20 percent of its value on Wednesday after the government announced its flotation after 13 years of being pegged to a basket of currencies.
